I have a nerdoctaxe and it's saying vreg over heat for some reason
Searched the web · NerdOctaxe Gamma "VREG OVERHEATED" Guru Meditation

Hi there,

Thanks for the photos. I've looked at both, and they show the problem clearly.

On the miner's screen there's a red "VREG OVERHEATED, Guru Meditation #····" message, and the hashrate reads 0.0 GH/s. Your web dashboard shows the same thing at 0.00 GH/s, with 8,976 GH/s expected. Most of the readings look healthy. The power supply is delivering 12.1 V, and the voltage regulator is cool at 33.7 °C, which is nowhere near overheating. Both fans are running at 100%. Your pool connection works too: 9 shares accepted on mining-dutch and none rejected. The one thing that's wrong is that the ASIC voltage is 0.00 V and the current is 0.00 A. The voltage regulator is refusing to power the chips. The miner isn't actually hot. The regulator has tripped a protection and stayed locked in that state.

I couldn't find an official explanation of the #···· code. What I did find is a very similar NerdOctaxe Gamma case on the firmware's GitHub page. That owner reported that
after reconnecting it, the display immediately showed "VREG OVERHEATED"
, and
all eight ASICs report 0 GH/s
, the same as yours. So I'd like to rule out a few simple things before I pass this to our hardware lead.

1. Do a full cold restart. Unplug the power supply from the wall, not just the miner, and leave it unplugged for 5 minutes. Check that nothing is blocking the heatsinks or the small regulator fan, then plug it back in. If the red error comes back, please take a short video from the moment you plug it in until the error appears.
2. Send me the firmware version. Open the miner's web page at 10.0.0.52 and look in the menu on the left (Settings or System). It starts with "v1.0...".
3. Send a clear photo of the serial number sticker or label on the board.
4. Tell me your order number, or the email address you used for the order, so your findings are linked to the right unit.

Don't change any voltage or frequency settings while it's in this state. If you ever notice a burning smell, smoke or a hot plug, unplug it right away and leave it unplugged.

Once I have these, I can finish my check and pass everything to our hardware lead. If you'd like to chat with the community in the meantime, you can join our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). He's very active there.

Talk soon,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
